question: A 41-year-old man is brought to the emergency room after a blunt-force injury to the abdomen. His pulse is 130/min and blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg. Ultrasound of the abdomen shows a large amount of blood in the hepatorenal recess and the pelvis. Which of the following responses by the kidney is most likely?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Blunt-force injury to abdomen" -> "Hypovolemic shock" -> "Decreased renal perfusion" -> "Activation of renin-angiotensin system" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Blunt-force injury to abdomen" -> "Hemorrhagic shock" -> "Decreased blood volume" -> "Compensatory mechanisms activated" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Blunt-force injury to abdomen" -> "Significant blood loss" -> "Decreased glomerular filtration rate" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption to conserve volume" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Blunt-force injury to abdomen" -> "Severe hypotension" -> "Reduced renal blood flow" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Blunt-force injury to abdomen" -> "Large volume of blood in abdomen" -> "Decreased effective circulating volume" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption" -> 80%
analysis: In the context of hypovolemic shock due to blunt-force abdominal injury, the kidneys respond to decreased perfusion and blood volume by activating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). This leads to increased sodium reabsorption in the renal tubules to help retain water and restore blood volume. Therefore, the most likely response by the kidney in this scenario is increased sodium reabsorption (option opc). The other options do not align with the physiological response to hypovolemia and shock.
normal_results: Abdominal compartment syndrome CAUSES Abnormal renal function
